title: Miscellaneous Provisions
outcomes: Apply restrictions on cash loans, deposits and receipts.
Apply e-payment facility and repayment rules.
Apply provisions on void transfers and provisional attachment.
Apply reporting, representation and procedural provisions.

meta.exam_tip: Identify whether the cash is a loan, a receipt or a repayment; each has its own section and penalty.

concepts.title: Restrictions on cash loans, deposits and receipts
body: Section 185: no person may take or accept a loan, deposit or specified sum (advance for transfer of immovable property) of ₹20,000 or more — counting the new amount, any outstanding balance, or both — otherwise than by account payee cheque or draft, ECS or prescribed electronic modes. A ₹2 lakh limit applies to transactions between primary agricultural credit societies or rural development banks and their members. Government, banks, post office savings banks, government companies and notified institutions are excluded, as are transactions where both parties have only agricultural income and no taxable income.

Section 186: no person may receive ₹2 lakh or more in cash in aggregate from a person in a day, for a single transaction, or for one event or occasion where the money comes from the same person. Receipts by Government, banks and specified bodies, and receipts covered by section 185, are excluded.
Penalties equal to the amount involved are levied under sections 450 and 451 respectively.
concepts.analogy: Large cash loans and receipts cost the full amount as penalty.
concepts.work: Cash of ₹2.4 lakh received over three days for one wedding is caught by section 186.

concepts.title: Electronic payment facility and repayments
body: Section 187: a person carrying on business with turnover above ₹50 crore in the preceding year must provide prescribed electronic payment facilities; it does not apply where at least 95% of receipts are in non-cash modes and the business is B2B. Failure attracts ₹5,000 per day (section 452).

Section 188: no branch of a bank, co-operative society, firm or other person may repay a loan, deposit or specified advance of ₹20,000 or more (including interest, and aggregated with the person's other such amounts) otherwise than by specified modes; ₹2 lakh for PACS/PCARD transactions with members.
Penalty under section 453 equals the amount repaid. Prescribed electronic modes include credit and debit cards, net banking, IMPS, UPI, RTGS, NEFT, BHIM Aadhaar Pay and specified CBDC wallets.
concepts.analogy: Big businesses must accept digital payments; big repayments must be digital.
concepts.work: A retailer that skips e-payment facilities for 20 days faces ₹1 lakh of penalty.

concepts.title: Protection of revenue: void transfers and attachment
body: Section 499: during pending proceedings or after their completion before notice of demand, a charge or transfer by the assessee of assets (exceeding ₹10,000 in value) is void against tax claims, unless made for adequate consideration without notice of the proceedings, or with the AO's permission.

Section 500: the AO may provisionally attach property during assessment or reassessment proceedings to protect revenue, with approval of the PCIT/CIT and other specified authorities; the attachment lasts six months, extendable to two years, and can be revoked on furnishing a bank guarantee. The AO may refer the property to a Valuation Officer.
Sections 501 to 504 deal with service of notices, including on HUFs after partition, dissolved firms and discontinued businesses.
concepts.analogy: The revenue can freeze assets to protect a likely demand.
concepts.work: A transfer of a flat to a relative for no consideration during scrutiny is void against tax claims.

concepts.title: Reporting, representation and general provisions
body: Section 507 requires specified persons to file statements of reportable financial transactions (e.g. large cash deposits, mutual fund and property purchases) within prescribed time; section 508 covers reportable accounts under international exchange agreements; crypto-asset service providers report under section 509. Penalties apply for non-filing or inaccurate statements.

Section 515: an assessee may appear through an authorised representative — a relative, regular employee, banking company officer, chartered accountant, legal practitioner, income-tax practitioner or other prescribed person — subject to disqualifications such as government service dismissal or professional misconduct.

Section 523: notices are not invalid merely because of a mistake or defect, if in substance they conform to the Act; participation in proceedings bars challenging service. Section 536 repeals the 1961 Act with savings for pending matters.
concepts.analogy: Reporting, representation and procedural fairness complete the framework.
concepts.work: A CA can appear on behalf of a client before the AO.

jobs.title: Cash-compliance audit
jobs.situation: A dealer's ledger shows several cash loans and customer receipts.
steps: List cash loans and deposits at or above ₹20,000.
Aggregate receipts per day, transaction and event.
Report in the tax audit and advise the client.
jobs.takeaway: Aggregation rules catch split cash transactions.

viva.q: What is a specified sum for section 185?
viva.model: Any advance taken for an immovable property deal, even if the deal later falls through.

viva.q: Name three ways section 186 aggregates receipts.
viva.model: Per person per day, per single transaction, and per event or occasion from a person.

viva.q: When can provisional attachment be revoked?
viva.model: When the assessee furnishes a bank guarantee of the required amount.

viva.q: What is a statement of reportable financial transactions?
viva.model: A statement filed by specified persons reporting large transactions such as cash deposits and property purchases.

viva.q: Is a notice invalid due to a minor defect?
viva.model: It remains valid if in substance it conforms to the Act, under section 523.
